label: 720XP-48Y6
description: Arista CCS-720XP-48Y6 - 1RU Cognitive Campus leaf: 48x 1G RJ45 PoE+ (10M-1G, Ethernet1-48) plus 6x 25G SFP28 (Ethernet49-54). 982 W of PoE with the single 1050 W supply it ships with.

poe.note: Arista's own row for CCS-720XP-48Y6: "PoE Power Budget Single / Dual PSU 982 W / 1850 W" (supported supply PWR-1021-AC, 68 W / 93 W typical / maximum excluding PoE). The switch ships with one 1050 W supply, so 982 W is the figure recorded here and the 1850 W two-supply ceiling is noted rather than used. Per port the datasheet caps the copper group at 30 W (802.3af/at), which is what the 48 template ports declare.

notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-20. Arista CCS-720XP data sheet "https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/CCS-720XP-Datasheet.pdf": "720XP-48Y6 - 48 x 10M-1GbE RJ45 @ 30W - Uplinks: 6x 25G", with the series described as "Managed 802.3af/at/bt power services ... up to 90W per RJ45 port" (90 W is the 48TXH-2C-S mGig port, not this one). Ordering information names "CCS-720XP-48Y6-F ... 48 x 10/100M-1G PoE, 6 x 25G SFP switch, front to rear air, 1 x 1050W AC". Arista 720XP/722XPM 1RU quick start guide "https://www.arista.com/en/qsg-720xp-series-1ru/720xp-series-1ru-overview" prints the budget row quoted in `poe.note`. The six uplinks are SFP28 cages (25G SFP in the vendor's table), so they source no power; only Ethernet1-48 are PSE ports. This spec used to describe PoE+ in prose while declaring no `poe-pse` capability and no budget, so the box powered nothing and `show power inline` answered that no port on it could supply power. Connectors and rates added 2026-11-24 from the same sheet: the 1G Platforms specification table gives "10M-1G UTP (30W 802.3af/at)" = 48 and "1G or 10G or 25G SFP" = 6, which is where the rj45 cage on the copper ports and the SFP28 cage with speedCaps [1000,10000,25000] on Ethernet49-54 come from. Before this, the six uplinks were declared as 25G copper ethernet with no cage at all, so a 25G "RJ45" was offered to the cabled model, and the 48 template ports named no connector or rate list. The PoE figures were already right (982 W from the "1Default Available PoE Power (Typ/Min) 982 W / 957 W" row) and are unchanged.
